direction: Search genuinely different structured basins de novo and only use best.npy as a fallback benchmark: generate a candidate pool from 6D lattice/algebraic vectors (all normalised nonzero integer vectors with coordinates in {-2,-1,0,1,2} and small support, plus all signed permutations of patterns such as (1,1,1,1,0,0)/2, (2,1,1,0,0,0)/sqrt(6), (1,1,1,0,0,0)/sqrt(3)), greedily select 250 points minimising the running maximum cosine, run discrete swap improvement (try replacing each selected point by pool vectors that lower the number of pairs within 1e-5 of the max), and also run an antipodal variant selecting 125 lines and duplicating with signs; spend at most 60 seconds on several such constructions, continuously polish the best two with annealed LogSumExp, and return whichever of the structured result or loaded best.npy has the lower verified max cosine.

idea: Target the single bottleneck pair with frozen-background pair/single-point smooth-max micro-optimization interleaved with global annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS basin-hopping and trust-region LP equalization of the dense plateau.
Collectively lower the broad ~1300-pair near-active plateau with moderate-beta LogSumExp plus large-neighborhood void reinsertion and uphill basin walking instead of single-pair whack-a-mole.
Cluster excision plus joint deep-hole regrowth of the bottleneck component with greedy far-point insertion and block re-optimisation.
direction: Perform cluster excision and joint deep-hole regrowth, not single-point reinsertion: form the graph of pairs with cosine above max-2e-5, take the connected component containing the worst pair, remove 20-35 of its points (always including the two bottleneck points), freeze the remaining ~215 points, and regrow the removed block jointly by repeatedly proposing 8,192 random sphere candidates, choosing the candidate minimising its maximum cosine to the frozen plus already-regrown points, refining each candidate by 60 iterations of single-point smooth-minimax descent, and after every 5 insertions jointly re-optimising the whole inserted block against the frozen set; repeat with several RNG seeds and excision sizes (15, 25, 40), then apply a short collective polish, keeping this strictly time-boxed to ~140 seconds with best.npy as fallback.

idea: Walk along floppy modes of the near-contact graph to a new topology then re-polish.
direction: Escape along floppy modes of the near-contact graph instead of random kicks: build the linearised contact matrix A (rows for pairs with slack <5e-6, entries B_i^T x_j and B_j^T x_i in tangent coordinates, expected shape roughly 1,300x1,250), compute its 25-40 smallest singular vectors with scipy.sparse.linalg.svds, and take large retracted steps of size 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 along random combinations of those vectors, accepting a step if the new max cosine is at most best+2e-4 before re-polishing with short beta=4000 then 15000 LogSumExp runs. Loop over random floppy directions for ~120 seconds, always returning to the incumbent on failure and keeping any polished configuration below the incumbent; these moves travel along the plateau to a different contact topology rather than fighting the single worst pair head-on.

idea: Exact active-set equalisation in fixed tangent coordinates with penalty least-squares on the true nonlinear retraction to tie the near-active plateau.
direction: Replace LogSumExp-plus-LP polishing with exact active-set equalisation in tangent coordinates: for each point build a 6x5 orthonormal tangent basis (null space of x_i), giving 1,250 variables u plus a scalar t, retract by x_i(u)=normalise(x_i+B_i u_i), and minimise t with scipy SLSQP or penalty least-squares subject to the exact nonlinear constraints <x_i(u),x_j(u)> <= t for all pairs with slack <3e-5 (cap at the 4,000 tightest, sparse Jacobian formed from B_i^T x_j and B_j^T x_i). Run a threshold ladder 1e-4 -> 1e-5 -> 1e-6, re-extracting the active set each time, until the tightest ~1,200-1,500 pairs are tied to <1e-10 or t stops decreasing, and report/keep the result only if it beats best.npy; this directly tests whether the plateau hides a substantially lower true local optimum that smoothed objectives cannot reach.

idea: True active-set SQP in tangent coordinates with HiGHS LP, trust-region adaptation and exact retracted line search to equalise the plateau.
direction: Finish this basin with a true active-set SQP instead of truncated smooth/LP steps. From `best.npy`, build a $6\times5$ tangent basis $Q_i$ per point (variables $1250$), take all pairs within $10^{-5}$ of the max ($\sim$1,600 pairs, not a 4,000-cap subsample), and repeatedly solve with HiGHS: minimise $t$ s.t. $c_{ij}+\langle x_j,Q_i u_i\rangle+\langle x_i,Q_j u_j\rangle \le t$ for active pairs and $\|u\|_\infty\le\rho$, $\rho$ adapted $10^{-4}\!\to\!10^{-2}$; after each step do an exact line search over $\alpha\in\{0.25,0.5,1,2\}$ on the retracted points, add every pair that comes within $10^{-6}$ of the new max, and drop pairs whose LP dual multiplier is zero for three consecutive iterations. Stop only when the LP predicts $t\ge-10^{-12}$ at $\rho=10^{-5}$ (a certified local optimum with its stress multipliers saved for comparison), return that if below `best.npy`, else the fallback; this either squeezes the real remaining $\sim10^{-6}$ out of the plateau or proves this basin is dead.

idea: Build hyperoctahedral-symmetric codes from analytic signed-permutation orbits plus free points and polish the best with symmetry-breaking Adam and LP.
direction: Search structured symmetric codes that the unstructured record cannot reach. Use the signed-permutation (hyperoctahedral) group on $\mathbb{R}^6$: parametrise a handful of seed vectors (e.g. permutations/signings of $(a,b,c,0,0,0)$, $(a,b,c,d,0,0)$, $(a,a,b,b,c,0)$), generate their orbits (sizes 12–240, deduplicated by rounding to $10^{-8}$), and select orbit combinations totalling exactly 250, filling any remainder with 2–10 free points. Optimise only the seed parameters plus free points (typically $<$40 variables) with L-BFGS-B on a $\beta=2000$ LogSumExp objective, enumerate a few dozen orbit combinations within $\sim$100 s, then break the symmetry with a full 250-point Adam+LP polish of the best combination. Exact orbit symmetry forces hundreds of contacts to be tied by construction, supplying the equalised contact network the incumbent lacks.

idea: Cardinality homotopy growth from N=180 with greedy deep-hole insertion and annealed smoothing to reach a different jammed basin at N=250.
direction: Reach a different basin by cardinality homotopy — grow a code from small $N$ instead of perturbing $N=250$. Optimise $N=180$ from a random start (easy, max cosine far below target), then insert points one at a time: at each step sample 100,000 random unit vectors plus antipodes/perturbed copies of existing points, pick the candidate minimising its maximum cosine to the current code, refine it by single-point smooth minimax against the fixed code (60 steps, $\beta=3000$), then run a brief all-points Adam polish (100 steps) every 10 insertions. Continue to $N=250$, then do a final annealed Adam ($\beta:400\to8000$) and LP polish; run two independent growth seeds if time permits and return the best, with `best.npy` as fallback only if neither beats it. Because early points lock in a contact topology before the code becomes jammed, the final adjacency graph should differ qualitatively from the record's plateau.

idea: Alternate penalty equalisation of the ~1300-pair plateau in fixed tangent coordinates with trust-region LP descent to reach a jammed isostatic optimum.

Escape the isostatic plateau along its floppy modes by building the plateau-pair Jacobian, stepping along its smallest singular vectors with curved retractions, then Adam LogSumExp and LP polishing only topologically distinct basins.
direction: Escape along spectral floppy modes of the plateau graph, not by random excision. Build the Jacobian $A$ ($\sim$1,300 plateau pairs within $2\times10^{-6}$ $\times$ 1,250 tangent coordinates), compute its 30 smallest right singular vectors via `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`, and for each mode and each sign take curved steps of angular size $\{0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2\}$ rad (retract $x_i\leftarrow \cos(\theta_i)x_i+\sin(\theta_i)\hat u_i$ per point), followed by a short Adam LogSumExp polish ($\beta:500\to5000$, 300 steps). Score each result by its exact max cosine and by a hash of its contact adjacency at $10^{-4}$ tolerance, keep only candidates whose adjacency differs from the incumbent in $\ge$5% of edges, and LP-polish the two most distinct improvers in the remaining time. This targets collective motions that lower the top pair and the plateau simultaneously, which single-pair and block moves cannot express.

idea: Alternate Riesz-energy global rearrangement with moderate-beta smooth-minimax equalisation plus worst-point deep-hole reinsertion to lower the whole ~1300-pair shell, finished by high-beta descent and trust-region LP squeeze.

Large-neighbourhood surgery that excises rattlers/low-contact points and regrows them by deep-hole insertion plus block LogSumExp optimisation, accepted with annealing to change basin before final LP jamming.
Stress-certify the near-contact shell with a sparse dual HiGHS LP and either descend along the primal trust-region direction or excise weak contacts and re-polish.
direction: Perform an exact stress-certification and equalisation analysis of the near-contact shell instead of ordinary score polishing. Load `best.npy`, collect all pairs with cosine above $M-10^{-6}$ (expected $\sim1300$–1500), construct Householder tangent bases vectorised with `einsum`, and solve the dual equilibrium problem for pair weights $w_p\ge t$, $\sum_p w_p=1$, and $\sum_{p\ni i} w_p Q_i^\top x_j=0$ for every point, maximising $t$ with a sparse HiGHS LP. If $t\le0$ or the LP is infeasible, extract the associated primal tangent descent direction, retract it with a decreasing trust-region ladder ($10^{-4},3\cdot10^{-5},10^{-5},3\cdot10^{-6}$) and exact line search; if a strictly positive stress exists, certify this basin as locally blocked and deliberately delete the lowest-weight 5–10% of shell contacts before re-polishing. Build all sparse matrices by vectorised COO index arithmetic, never by looping over pairs, timebox the LP work to 150 seconds, and always return the best exactly evaluated configuration.

idea: Search hyperoctahedral symmetric codes with parametric permutation orbits plus free points via beta=2000 LogSumExp L-BFGS-B, then break symmetry with full Adam and LP polish.
direction: Search structured symmetric codes that the unstructured record cannot reach. Use the signed-permutation (hyperoctahedral) group on $\mathbb{R}^6$: parametrise a handful of seed vectors (e.g. permutations/signings of $(a,b,c,0,0,0)$, $(a,b,c,d,0,0)$, $(a,a,b,b,c,0)$), generate their orbits (sizes 12–240, deduplicated by rounding to $10^{-8}$), and select orbit combinations totalling exactly 250, filling any remainder with 2–10 free points. Optimise only the seed parameters plus free points (typically $<$40 variables) with L-BFGS-B on a $\beta=2000$ LogSumExp objective, enumerate a few dozen orbit combinations within $\sim$100 s, then break the symmetry with a full 250-point Adam+LP polish of the best combination. Exact orbit symmetry forces hundreds of contacts to be tied by construction, supplying the equalised contact network the incumbent lacks.

idea: Coordinated bottleneck surgery freezing the complement of the $M-10^{-4}$ neighbourhood of the maximal pair and jointly reoptimising it with ramped LogSumExp L-BFGS, with $a,b$ restarts from 20k jointly-scored deep-hole pairs plus opposite-tangent pushes, accepting only global improvements followed by 5-step sparse LP polish.
direction: Attack the isolated bottleneck pair by coordinated multi-point surgery rather than moving single rattlers. Identify the unique maximal pair $(a,b)$ and the union $S$ of points having cosine $>M-10^{-4}$ with $a$ or $b$, typically 20–50 points; freeze the other points and jointly reoptimise all points in $S$ on $S^5$ using LogSumExp minimax L-BFGS with $\beta$ ramped through $10^3,3\cdot10^3,10^4,3\cdot10^4$, including interactions within $S$ and with the frozen set. Restart $a$ and $b$ from jointly sampled deep-hole pairs—generate at least 20,000 random unit-vector pairs, score each by its maximum cosine to the frozen set and to each other, refine the best 20 pairs—and also try displacing $a,b$ in opposite tangent directions and along their difference direction. Accept a surgery only if the exact global maximum improves, then apply at most five sparse tangent-LP polish iterations with a $10^{-5}$ active window; repeat with different random seeds until a 160-second deadline.

idea: Batched p-energy homotopy with 24 vectorised replicas, rigidity-based evolutionary reseeding, and sparse tangent-LP polish of three distinct candidates.
direction: Run a genuinely fresh batched global search based on $p$-energy homotopy and select candidates by rigidity, not merely by intermediate score. Simulate at least 24 independent $250\times6$ replicas simultaneously with vectorised numpy gradient descent, minimising $\left(\sum_{i<j}\max(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle,0)^p\right)^{1/p}$ or an equivalent soft-max energy while ramping $p$ or $\beta$ through a schedule such as $20,50,100,200,500,1000$; initialise replicas from random points, random orthogonal transformations and subset crossovers of the incumbent, and differently perturbed incumbents. Periodically compute for each replica the number of pairs within $10^{-4}$ of its maximum, the minimum contact degree, and whether its contact graph is connected, and favour replicas approaching at least five near-contacts per point. Polish the best three structurally distinct replicas with the sparse tangent LP, compare them exactly with the incumbent, and return the best configuration before 175 seconds.

idea: Alternate annealed LogSumExp Adam equalisation with adaptive trust-region LP descent and small random kicks to change active topology while preserving the jammed plateau.
